passages.text: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of the sons of Korah.
passages.sermon:
This is a psalm.
The sons of Korah wrote this psalm.
The choirmaster leads the music for this psalm.

passages.text: Hear this, all you peoples; listen, all inhabitants of the world, both low and high, rich and poor alike.
passages.sermon:
This is a psalm.
The sons of Korah wrote this psalm.
The psalm is for the choirmaster.
All peoples must hear this message.
All inhabitants of the world must listen.
This message is for everyone.
This message is for both low and high people.
This message is for both rich and poor people.
No one is left out.
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֬חַ׀ לִבְנֵי־ קֹ֬רַח מִזְמֽוֹר׃ שִׁמְעוּ־ זֹ֭את כָּל־ הָֽעַמִּ֑ים הַ֝אֲזִ֗ינוּ כָּל־ יֹ֥שְׁבֵי חָֽלֶד׃ גַּם־ בְּנֵ֣י אָ֭דָם גַּם־ בְּנֵי־ אִ֑ישׁ יַ֝֗חַד עָשִׁ֥יר וְאֶבְיֽוֹן׃

passages.text: My mouth will impart wisdom, and the meditation of my heart will bring understanding.
passages.sermon:
The sons of Korah wrote this psalm.
They speak to all people.
They say, “My mouth will speak wisdom.”
“My heart will think about understanding.”
passages.original: פִּ֭י יְדַבֵּ֣ר חָכְמ֑וֹת וְהָג֖וּת לִבִּ֣י תְבוּנֽוֹת׃

passages.text: I will incline my ear to a proverb; I will express my riddle with the harp: Why should I fear in times of trouble, when wicked usurpers surround me?
passages.sermon:
The sons of Korah wrote this psalm.
They speak to all people in the world.
They want everyone to listen.
They say, “I will listen carefully to a proverb.”
A proverb is a wise saying.
They say, “I will open my riddle with the harp.”
A riddle is a difficult question or mystery.
They use music to share their message.
They ask, “Why should I be afraid in days of trouble?”
They face times when evil surrounds them.
Wicked people try to trap them.
They wonder why they should fear in these times.
passages.original: אַטֶּ֣ה לְמָשָׁ֣ל אָזְנִ֑י אֶפְתַּ֥ח בְּ֝כִנּ֗וֹר חִידָתִֽי׃ לָ֣מָּה אִ֭ירָא בִּ֣ימֵי רָ֑ע עֲוֺ֖ן עֲקֵבַ֣י יְסוּבֵּֽנִי׃

passages.text: They trust in their wealth and boast in their great riches.
passages.sermon:
Some people trust in their wealth.
They rely on their money.
They boast about their great riches.
They take pride in how much they own.
passages.original: הַבֹּטְחִ֥ים עַל־ חֵילָ֑ם וּבְרֹ֥ב עָ֝שְׁרָ֗ם יִתְהַלָּֽלוּ׃

passages.text: No man can possibly redeem his brother or pay his ransom to God.
passages.sermon: No man can redeem his brother.\r\nNo man can pay a ransom to God for another person.
passages.original: אָ֗ח לֹא־ פָדֹ֣ה יִפְדֶּ֣ה אִ֑ישׁ לֹא־ יִתֵּ֖ן לֵאלֹהִ֣ים כָּפְרֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For the redemption of his soul is costly, and never can payment suffice, that he should live on forever and not see decay.
passages.sermon:
A person cannot redeem his own soul.
The price to save a soul is very high.
No one can pay enough to redeem a soul.
No payment is ever enough.
No one can live forever by paying a ransom.
No one can avoid death and decay by wealth or payment.
passages.original: וְ֭יֵקַר פִּדְי֥וֹן נַפְשָׁ֗ם וְחָדַ֥ל לְעוֹלָֽם׃ וִֽיחִי־ ע֥וֹד לָנֶ֑צַח לֹ֖א יִרְאֶ֣ה הַשָּֽׁחַת׃

passages.text: For it is clear that wise men die, and the foolish and the senseless both perish and leave their wealth to others.
passages.sermon:
Every person will die.
Wise men die.
Foolish men die.
Senseless men die.
All of them perish.
They cannot keep their wealth.
They leave their wealth to other people.
passages.original: כִּ֤י יִרְאֶ֨ה׀ חֲכָ֘מִ֤ים יָמ֗וּתוּ יַ֤חַד כְּסִ֣יל וָבַ֣עַר יֹאבֵ֑דוּ וְעָזְב֖וּ לַאֲחֵרִ֣ים חֵילָֽם׃

passages.text: Their graves are their eternal homes— their dwellings for endless generations— even though their lands were their namesakes.
passages.sermon:
People die.
Their graves become their homes forever.
Their graves are their dwellings for all generations.
They once named lands after themselves.
But now they live in the ground forever.
passages.original: קִרְבָּ֤ם בָּתֵּ֨ימוֹ׀ לְֽעוֹלָ֗ם מִ֭שְׁכְּנֹתָם לְדֹ֣ר וָדֹ֑ר קָֽרְא֥וּ בִ֝שְׁמוֹתָ֗ם עֲלֵ֣י אֲדָמֽוֹת׃

passages.text: But a man, despite his wealth, cannot endure; he is like the beasts that perish.
passages.sermon:
A man may have great wealth.
He cannot last forever.
He will not remain.
He is like the animals that die.
He perishes as they do.
passages.original: וְאָדָ֣ם בִּ֭יקָר בַּל־ יָלִ֑ין נִמְשַׁ֖ל כַּבְּהֵמ֣וֹת נִדְמֽוּ׃

passages.text: This is the fate of the self-confident and their followers who endorse their sayings. Selah Like sheep they are destined for Sheol. Death will be their shepherd. The upright will rule them in the morning, and their form will decay in Sheol, far from their lofty abode.
passages.sermon:
Self-confident people trust in themselves.
Their followers agree with their words.
This is their fate.
They will go to the grave like sheep.
Death will lead them.
Righteous people will rule over them in the morning.
Their bodies will rot in the grave.
They will be far from their proud homes.
passages.original: זֶ֣ה דַ֭רְכָּם כֵּ֣סֶל לָ֑מוֹ וְאַחֲרֵיהֶ֓ם׀ בְּפִיהֶ֖ם יִרְצ֣וּ סֶֽלָה׃ כַּצֹּ֤אן׀ לִֽשְׁא֣וֹל שַׁתּוּ֮ מָ֤וֶת יִ֫רְעֵ֥ם וַיִּרְדּ֘וּ בָ֤ם יְשָׁרִ֨ים׀ לַבֹּ֗קֶר וְצִירָם לְבַלּ֥וֹת שְׁא֗וֹל מִזְּבֻ֥ל לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But God will redeem my life from Sheol, for He will surely take me to Himself. Selah Do not be amazed when a man grows rich, when the splendor of his house increases.
passages.sermon:
God will save my soul from Sheol.
God will take me to Himself.
Do not fear when a man becomes rich.
Do not fear when the glory of his house grows.
passages.original: אַךְ־ אֱלֹהִ֗ים יִפְדֶּ֣ה נַ֭פְשִׁי מִֽיַּד־ שְׁא֑וֹל כִּ֖י יִקָּחֵ֣נִי סֶֽלָה׃ אַל־ תִּ֭ירָא כִּֽי־ יַעֲשִׁ֣ר אִ֑ישׁ כִּֽי־ יִ֝רְבֶּה כְּב֣וֹד בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For when he dies, he will carry nothing away; his abundance will not follow him down.
passages.sermon:
A man may have great wealth.
He cannot take anything with him when he dies.
His riches will not go with him to the grave.
His honor will not follow him after death.
passages.original: כִּ֤י לֹ֣א בְ֭מוֹתוֹ יִקַּ֣ח הַכֹּ֑ל לֹא־ יֵרֵ֖ד אַחֲרָ֣יו כְּבוֹדֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Though in his lifetime he blesses his soul— and men praise you when you prosper— he will join the generation of his fathers, who will never see the light of day.
passages.sermon:
A man may bless himself while he lives.
Other people may praise you when you do well.
But he will go to his ancestors after he dies.
He will never see the light again.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ נַ֭פְשׁוֹ בְּחַיָּ֣יו יְבָרֵ֑ךְ וְ֝יוֹדֻ֗ךָ כִּי־ תֵיטִ֥יב לָֽךְ׃ תָּ֭בוֹא עַד־ דּ֣וֹר אֲבוֹתָ֑יו עַד־ נֵ֝֗צַח לֹ֣א יִרְאוּ־ אֽוֹר׃

passages.text: A man who has riches without understanding is like the beasts that perish.
passages.sermon:
A man may have riches.
He may have honor.
If he does not have understanding, he is like the animals.
The animals die and are gone.
A man without understanding will also perish like them.
passages.original: אָדָ֣ם בִּ֭יקָר וְלֹ֣א יָבִ֑ין נִמְשַׁ֖ל כַּבְּהֵמ֣וֹת נִדְמֽוּ׃
